## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double anonymized: the live about page says "All peer review is double anonymized and original articles are typically reviewed by two expert referees" (https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/cphp20/about-this-journal, read 2026-11-24; same wording in the 2025-06-27 copy). The live instructions say that once the editor has judged suitability the paper is double blind peer reviewed by independent, anonymous expert referees (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=cphp20&page=instructions, read 2026-11-24). The 2022-01-20 instructions copy stated that book reviews and review essays are not peer reviewed by policy (not re-checked on the live page). The editor's 2022 post says original research papers get at least two independent expert reviews |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No source read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No source read |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev (n=3): 1.7 review rounds on average and 2.7 review reports on average (https://scirev.org/journal/philosophical-psychology/). Survey respondents (APA Journal Survey Project, n=65, https://apasurvey.philx.org/journals/794): of 65 initial verdicts, 3 acceptances, 20 rejections, 38 revise-and-resubmit and 4 conditional acceptances; of 37 later verdicts, 29 acceptances, 4 rejections and 4 withdrawals; average 1.9 reviewers. The page's own "overall acceptance rate" is 49.23%, a survey-defined figure |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No source found |

Editors and reviewers must not upload unpublished manuscripts to AI tools, and reviewers may not use AI to analyse or summarise submissions. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |

## Format

> Source for the general rules: the journal's live instructions for authors (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=cphp20&page=instructions), read in a real browser on 2026-11-24; the page prints no date. Retrieved 2026-11-24. The archived copy of 2022-01-20 is older.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | The archived instructions list two types: original articles and book reviews; English only. The editor's 2021 announcement lists original research articles, commentaries and book reviews (https://dailynous.com/2021/10/15/journal-news-philosophical-psychology-and-neuroethics-guest-post/). OpenAlex type counts for 2021-2026: 691 articles, 90 book reviews, 32 editorials |
| **Word limit** | "A typical paper for this journal should be no more than 10,000 words, inclusive of the abstract, tables, references, figure captions", and authors are asked to include a word count (live instructions, read 2026-11-24). Measured: median article length 24 pages (quartiles 20 to 27) over 689 records with a parseable page range (OpenAlex biblio fields, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The live instructions word it as a typical-paper ceiling ("a typical paper"); no exception procedure is stated |
| **Abstract limit** | "An unstructured abstract of 200 words"; keywords are listed in the structure order (live instructions, read 2026-11-24; the page text read does not repeat the 6-keyword cap stated in the 2022-01-20 copy). Measured: abstract median 170 words (quartiles 134 to 193, maximum 309); 62 of 686 abstracts exceed 200 words (OpenAlex) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap found; references count inside the 10,000 words (live instructions, read 2026-11-24) |
| **Supplementary material** | A data sharing policy line: authors are encouraged, not required, to share the data supporting the paper and to deposit datasets in a recognised repository that mints a persistent identifier (live instructions, read 2026-11-24). The 2022-01-20 copy also named Figshare for supplemental material (not re-checked on the live page) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Resolution and editable-table requirements are given in the archived instructions; print colour figures are charged |
| **Style / submission format** | The live instructions say the title uses format-free submission; spelling can be US or UK English if consistent (the 2022-01-20 copy required American spelling); order: title page, abstract, keywords, main text, acknowledgments, declaration of interest statement, references, appendices, tables, figures; ScholarOne Manuscripts; an editable file is required at revision; the journal adds image descriptions (alt text) to informative images, and the publisher uses AI to draft them unless authors supply their own (live instructions, read 2026-11-24) |

### Orientation

> Counts below: OpenAlex records of type article for this journal dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-12-31 (691 records; 686, or 99%, carry an abstract), pulled through the works API (https://api.openalex.org/works, source S27428843) and matched locally by word-boundary regexes against title plus abstract. Percentages use 686 as the denominator. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Mixed, with a theoretical majority. "argue", "defend", "thesis" or "objection" appear in 406 of 686 abstracts (59.2%; regex `\bargue\w*\|\bdefend\w*\|\bthesis\b\|\bobjection\w*`); `\bparticipants\b\|\bsurvey\w*\|\bvignette\w*\|\bexperiment[s]? (?:with\|on\|in which)\b` matches 81 (11.8%), and of the 7 hits I read, 6 report participant data (e.g. https://doi.org/10.1080/09515089.2022.2046262, https://doi.org/10.1080/09515089.2023.2289451) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Both appear. Quantitative or statistical terms 35 of 686 (5.1%); qualitative or interview terms 29 (4.2%). Of the first 7 hits read for each term group, 4 of the quantitative (plus 1 borderline) and 4 of the qualitative (plus 1 borderline) were genuine studies; the others were name or concept uses (the title of a diagnostic manual, statistical learning mechanisms) |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The aims text names cognitive, social and affective sciences, neuroscience, comparative psychology, clinical psychology, psychopathology, psychiatry, psychoanalysis, educational and health psychology, moral psychology, phenomenology, history of psychology and experimental philosophy, and says contributors include neuroscientists, linguists, computer scientists, biologists and sociologists (Wayback copy 2025-06-27). Counts: psychiatry or mental-disorder terms 127 of 686 (18.5%), neuroscience and brain terms 85 (12.4%), "psycholog-" 177 (25.8%) |

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

> Evidence layers: OpenAlex keyword counts over 686 abstracts (regexes written in the cells); OpenAlex author-country counts over 820 works; the journal's aims text (Wayback copy 2025-06-27). Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Author countries of the 820 works in 2021-2026 (OpenAlex works with at least one author in the country; a work can count in several): United States 208, United Kingdom 179, Germany 82, Italy 48, Australia 45, Netherlands 40, Denmark 32, Spain 32, Canada 27, Belgium 23, Switzerland 23, China 22, France 22 (https://api.openalex.org/works, group_by authorships.countries) |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Rare by count: `\bdecoloni\w*\|\bIndigenous\b\|\bBuddhis\w*\|\bConfuci\w*\|\bDaoi\w*\|\bTaoi\w*\|\bAfrican philosoph\w*\|\bIslamic\b\|\bIndian\b\|\bChinese\b` matches 3 of 686 abstracts (0.4%). No editorial statement on non-Western traditions found |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Present. Feminist, gender or race terms (`\bfeminis\w*\|\bgender\w*\|\bracial\w*\|\brace\b\|\bracis\w*\|\boppress\w*`) 22 of 686 (3.2%); disability, queer or trans terms 10 (1.5%). The most cited article of the window concerns epistemic injustice in psychiatry (https://doi.org/10.1080/09515089.2022.2156333, 175 OpenAlex citations). The editor's 2022 post names an open call on understanding bias |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Naturalistic, cognitive-science-facing philosophy of mind and psychology. Concept, representation and content terms 245 of 686 (35.7%); perception, attention, memory or imagination 144 (21.0%); emotion or affect 139 (20.3%); consciousness or experience 134 (19.5%); free will, agency or intention 106 (15.5%); embodied, enactive or extended terms 52 (7.6%); predictive-processing terms 26 (3.8%); phenomenology 71 (10.3%). Historical names (James, Hume, Kant, Aristotle, Descartes, Husserl, Merleau-Ponty, Heidegger) 20 (2.9%). The aims text describes the journal as developing links between philosophy and the psychological sciences and publishing both empirical and conceptual work. No political position is stated on any page read |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One scope statement from the journal itself: contributions should develop and strengthen links between philosophy and the psychological sciences; the journal publishes empirical and conceptual work relevant to philosophical debate and philosophical work relevant to research in the psychological sciences (https://web.archive.org/web/20250627011527/https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/cphp20/about-this-journal, Wayback copy dated 2025-06-27; retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **What kind of engagement?** Engagement with both sides of the philosophy-psychology link, not a named theoretical school. The 2021 editor announcement says the scope stays the same, original research articles, commentaries and book reviews at the intersection of philosophy and the psychological sciences (https://dailynous.com/2021/10/15/journal-news-philosophical-psychology-and-neuroethics-guest-post/).
- **Article type and length**: original articles and book reviews, up to about 10,000 words including references, an unstructured 200-word abstract and up to 6 keywords (instructions copy dated 2022-01-20, https://web.archive.org/web/20220120065638/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=cphp20&show=instructions).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: four open calls on the 2025-11-30 home copy ("Ian Hacking and the Philosophy of Psychiatry", "Experimental argument analysis", "Imagination, Creativity and AI", "Philosophy through art, games, and fiction"; https://web.archive.org/web/20251130030340/https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/cphp20).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No page read states what happens to out-of-scope submissions, and no desk-rejection figure exists (SciRev "immediately rejected" n/a: https://scirev.org/journal/philosophical-psychology/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are OpenAlex article records dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-12-31 whose title or abstract matches the regex, over the 686 records with an abstract (99% of 691). Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. The aims text says the journal publishes empirical and conceptual work, which supports but does not by itself justify a 4. Where I read the hits and part were not uses of the method, the score is set one band lower and the row says so. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | `\bparticipants\b\|\bsurvey\w*\|\bvignette\w*\|\bexperiment[s]? (?:with\|on\|in which)\b\|\bn ?= ?\d+` 81 of 686 (11.8%); 6 of the 7 hits read are participant studies (e.g. https://doi.org/10.1080/09515089.2023.2289451, https://doi.org/10.1080/09515089.2022.2088340). The aims text names "experimental work" and "experimental philosophy" |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | `\bqualitative\b\|\binterview\w*\|\bethnograph\w*\|\bthematic analysis\b` 29 of 686 (4.2%); 4 of the first 7 hits read are clearly qualitative or interview studies and 1 is borderline (e.g. https://doi.org/10.1080/09515089.2022.2056009, https://doi.org/10.1080/09515089.2023.2197936) |
| Autoethnography | 1 | `\bautoethnograph\w*\|\bethnograph\w*` 1 of 686 abstracts |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | `\bargue\w*\|\bdefend\w*\|\bthesis\b\|\bobjection\w*` 406 of 686 (59.2%); `\bconceptual\w*\|\banalysis of\b\|\baccount of\b\|\btheory of\b` 251 (36.6%) |
| Statistical / quantitative analysis (added row) | 2 | `\bquantitative\b\|\bstatistic\w*\|\bregression\b\|\bsample size\b` 35 of 686 (5.1%), at the band boundary; 4 of the 7 hits read are genuine quantitative studies (e.g. N = 263 panel design, https://doi.org/10.1080/09515089.2023.2296585), so the lower band is used |
| Mixed methods | 1 | `\bmixed[- ]method\w*` 2 of 686 (0.3%) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 1 | `\bsystematic review\w*\|\bmeta-analys\w*\|\bscoping review\w*` 4 of 686 (0.6%) |
| Computational / simulation (added row) | 2 | `\bsimulation\w*\|\bcomputational\b\|\bagent-based\b` 33 of 686 (4.8%) |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Observed: 580 of 686 abstracts (84.5%) contain I, we, my, our or me under the regex `(?<![A-Za-z.(])(?:I (?=[a-z])\|We \|we \|My \|my \|Our \|our \|me\b)` (plural "we" may be generic). The most-cited items include https://doi.org/10.1080/09515089.2022.2160311 and https://doi.org/10.1080/09515089.2022.2156333. The archived instructions give no first-person rule |
| **Expected density** | Median 24 pages per article (quartiles 20 to 27; 689 of 691 records with a page range). Abstracts: median 170 words (quartiles 134 to 193, maximum 309). Source: https://api.openalex.org/works, retrieved 2026-11-23. Length ceiling about 10,000 words including references (archived instructions) |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Unstructured abstract of 200 words, optional graphical abstract, no more than 6 keywords (archived instructions, https://web.archive.org/web/20220120065638/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=cphp20&show=instructions) |
| **Writing style notes** | Archived instructions (2022-01-20): American spelling used consistently; double quotation marks; long quotations indented; English only; authors told to follow the quick style guidelines rather than copy published articles. The page also lists a generic section order (introduction, materials and methods, results, discussion) that is publisher template text. Because 59.2% of abstracts are argumentative and 11.8% report participant data, whether articles follow that order was not sampled |
| **Authorship pattern** | Of 690 OpenAlex article records with an author list: 430 single-author (62.3%), 154 two authors, 56 three, 50 four or more (https://api.openalex.org/works, retrieved 2026-11-23) |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the aims text says contributions should link philosophy and the psychological sciences (Framing Requirements, Wayback copy 2025-06-27). A paper with no engagement with that link is outside the stated scope.
- **Length**: a typical paper should not exceed 10,000 words including abstract, tables, references and figure captions (Format, live instructions read 2026-11-24); whether exceptions are granted is not stated.
- **Anonymisation**: double-anonymous review (Peer Review) means the manuscript must be prepared so that it can be read without author identity; the live instructions do not describe how beyond "double blind", and they warn that anonymity cannot be guaranteed for a manuscript shared on a preprint server (Preprint Policy, Peer Review).
- **AI use**: undisclosed AI use or AI-created or altered research results breach the publisher policy (AI Policy, https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: SciRev n=3 reports an average first review round of 5.2 months and 8.8 months total handling, against the publisher's 42 to 65 days for a decision (Review Cycle Time); the sources differ and n is small.
- **Competition**: publisher-reported acceptance rate 26%; the editor reports 12.4% for research articles in 2022 after 290 submissions in ten months (Metrics, Publication Frequency). The same post reports research-article submissions rising from 190 (2021) to 290 (first ten months of 2022).
- **Open access cost**: green deposit of the accepted manuscript is generally delayed 18 months for non-open-access articles under the publisher page (Preprint Policy; not confirmed for this journal); the APC for open access was not read.

### Best Suited For

- Philosophy of mind and cognition that engages empirical science: concept and representation terms 35.7%, perception and attention 21.0%, emotion 20.3%, consciousness 19.5% (Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Philosophy of psychiatry and mental health: psychiatry and mental-disorder terms 18.5%, and a current call on Ian Hacking and the philosophy of psychiatry (Sensitive Topics).
- Experimental philosophy and participant-based studies framed for a philosophical audience: 11.8% of abstracts report participant data, the aims text names experimental philosophy, and a current call is on experimental argument analysis (Methodological Preferences, Special issues).
- Sole-authored work: 62.3% of article records are single-author (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Purely formal or historical work with no psychological-science link: formal-proof terms 1.9% and named historical figures 2.9% (Methodological Preferences, Epistemological). The counts show rarity, not rejection.
- Decolonial, non-Western or political-conflict topics without a mind or psychology angle: 0.4% and 0.6% (Sensitive Topics); a frequency, not a stated exclusion.
- Authors with a manuscript well above 10,000 words including references: the live instructions give that as the typical ceiling (Format).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows below are topical neighbours that already exist in this corpus (philosophy of mind, psychology and psychiatry); they are not a claim about acceptance odds, and no fit evidence was collected for them in this pass.
